The Walls Brands Hit on Shopify and the German Platforms Answering Them

In this issue

  • The walls. Three option types per product. Shopify allows up to 2,048 variants on a product but only three option dimensions, and configurable goods run out of dimensions long before they run out of variants.
  • The shapes that hit the walls. The brands that hit those walls are the structurally complicated ones, whatever their size, and the names later in this issue show the shapes.
  • Four Germans, five walls. The API-ceilings wall has the least symmetric answer of the five, because it is a question of ownership more than product.
  • The elder German. The oldest name in the story is hybris. Before most of the platforms above existed it was selling commerce software to General Electric, Procter & Gamble, and Johnson & Johnson, and SAP paid about 1.5 billion dollars for it and rebranded it SAP Commerce Cloud.
  • Do the Germans do consumer? Spryker's front door sells to B2B enterprises, and SCAYLE spun off as About You's B2B division, so the reflex is to file the Germans away from anything a shopper touches, and the customer lists above say otherwise.
  • What switching costs. Leaving Shopify relocates the app tax, and the app tax framing explains where it goes.
  • Where I land. Shopify has an answer to all of this, and it is a fair one.
